Answer: B
Reason: The radiographic findings of a tubular opacity (representing a mucocoele or impacted bronchus) in the left upper lobe accompanied by adjacent hyperlucency (hyperinflation due to collateral air drift) are classic features of congenital bronchial atresia. This condition is typically an incidental finding in asymptomatic young adults, distinguishing it from infectious, allergic, or neoplastic processes which usually present with different clinical and radiological patterns.
